Your medchem team has a congeneric series against the primary target. Enzyme potency is comparable across the four analogues below (all single-digit nM), so the next-compound decision turns on developability, not potency. Synthesis capacity is limited: you can carry at most three forward and must drop at least one. Candidate structures are the four compounds below (SMILES available via their ADMET records).

Candidate compounds:
  C1: analogue C1  [ADMET-001]
  C2: analogue C2  [ADMET-006]
  C3: analogue C3  [ADMET-003]
  C4: analogue C4  [ADMET-013]

Run ADMET on the series, then recommend which analogues to advance and which single analogue to deprioritize, with its dominant liability. Finish with a DECISION block: advance: <labels> / deprioritize: <labels> / primary_liability: <name>.

Weighing the measured profiles, C3 carries the dominant hERG liability (herg); C1, C2, C4 have the cleaner profiles and advance.
DECISION:
  advance: C1, C2, C4
  deprioritize: C3
  primary_liability: hERG

You have a congeneric series against c-Met and a current lead (the reference ligand). Before committing synthesis you want relative binding free energies (ΔΔG vs the reference) to decide which analogues genuinely improve potency. More-negative ΔΔG = tighter binding than the lead; positive = weaker. Five analogues are shown.

Candidate compounds:
  L1: L1
  L2: L2
  L3: L3
  L4: L4
  L5: L5

Run RBFE/FEP on the series, then recommend which analogues to advance (those meaningfully tighter-binding than the lead) and which single analogue to deprioritize (clearly weaker). Finish with a DECISION block: advance: <labels> / deprioritize: <labels> / primary_liability: <name>.

Weighing the measured profiles, L5 carries the dominant weaker binding affinity liability (ddg); L1, L2 have the cleaner profiles and advance.
DECISION:
  advance: L1, L2
  deprioritize: L5
  primary_liability: weaker binding affinity
